summary: Repaired .1R.5.1's BLOCKING finding F1: AuthenticatedHumanPrincipal's HPAC-REQ-056 trusted-construction seal was enforced only inside __init__, so object.__new__(AuthenticatedHumanPrincipal) allocated a fully-populated, isinstance-true, PRODUCTION-assurance forged instance without ever running verify_human_authentication. Rather than trying to make object.__new__-allocated instances stop being isinstance-true (not achievable in pure Python -- object.__new__(cls) allocating a genuine instance of cls is definitionally what isinstance checks; it also bypasses any subclass __new__ override entirely, since it is a direct call to object's own unrelated method, not a call through the subclass's MRO), added a verifier-owned, identity-keyed provenance boundary: is_verifier_authenticated_principal(candidate), which checks membership in a new module-private, process-local registry (_AUTHENTIC_PRINCIPAL_REGISTRY) that only verify_human_authentication's own return path ever populates. A caller-manufactured lookalike -- via direct construction (even with the real module-private seal), object.__new__, a subclass attempt (now refused at class-definition time via __init_subclass__), copy.copy/copy.deepcopy/pickle (still TypeError via __reduce__, unchanged), manual __slots__ state copying, or reflection-based reconstruction -- is a different Python object and is therefore never a registry member, regardless of how many fields match a genuine result byte-for-byte. is_real_runtime_eligible and every other field remain plain data properties, not authority; the module docstring and class docstring now explicitly require every future consumer to call is_verifier_authenticated_principal before trusting them, since this module still has zero production consumers today and therefore no call site to update. The __init__ seal check was retained as defense-in-depth for the ordinary direct-construction mistake, but is documented as not the trust boundary. Subclassing is refused outright via __init_subclass__ since a subclass could otherwise define its own __init__ skipping the seal entirely. The registry is a plain (strong-reference) set rather than a weakref.WeakSet, because adding "__weakref__" to __slots__ (needed for weak references) would break .1R.5.1's preserved historical evidence test (test_verifier_result_attribute_copy_produces_a_distinguishable_object), which iterates the literal __slots__ tuple and setattrs every entry -- __weakref__ has no attribute setter. This is documented as an accepted, deliberate trade-off (verified results remain referenced for the process lifetime, not persisted, not serializable, not surviving restart) given zero production consumers exist today. F2/F3/F4 unchanged/deferred exactly as .1R.5.1 classified them (not technically coupled to F1). Added tests/test_hpac_verifier_repair_3w1r2b1r1115a2.py (20 new tests, all passing) covering every path in the governing prompt's checklist: direct constructor (with and without the real seal), object.__new__, subclass refusal, shallow/deep copy, pickle, manual slot-state copy, reflection, forged-with-identical-fields, non-principal inputs, cross-call non-equality, registry lifetime/strong-reference behavior, deterministic NON-REAL regression, and re-confirmed zero PB/runtime/Gate-9 imports and zero production consumers. .1R.5.1's own 29-test historical suite preserved completely unmodified: 27 of 29 still pass; the 2 that do not (test_object_dunder_new_bypasses_trusted_construction_seal, test_forged_via_object_new_would_report_real_runtime_eligible) assert postconditions (not isinstance(...), is_real_runtime_eligible is False on a hand-forged instance) that are not achievable by any construction-boundary fix in Python and are documented as permanently failing by design, not silently rewritten to match the implementation. F1: REPAIRED -- INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION PENDING -- NOT CLOSED. Recommends 149O.20L.7O.3W.1R.2B.1R.1.1R.5.2.1 (independent verification) next, pending separate explicit human authorization -- not pre-assigned by this phase per the no-invent-an-ID constraint. No B1/B7/N1/N2 repair; no PB/runtime-authority integration; no real FIDO2/UI; execution not enabled.
derived_correctness: The repair mechanism (identity-keyed registry rather than any field/seal-based check) was independently derived by first confirming, via direct interactive Python probing, that overriding AuthenticatedHumanPrincipal's own __new__ cannot close the documented attack, because the F1 reproduction calls object.__new__(AuthenticatedHumanPrincipal) directly -- a call to a different, unrelated method than any subclass override, bypassing the MRO entirely. This was independently confirmed against the actual installed module before writing any repair code (a subclass __new__ override was written experimentally, then confirmed by direct probe to have zero effect on the object.__new__(cls) call path, then removed in favor of the registry approach). Every §20/§21 adversarial path (direct construction with and without the real seal, object.__new__, subclass, copy, deepcopy, pickle, manual slot copy, reflection, forged-identical-fields) was independently reproduced against the repaired module and confirmed rejected by is_verifier_authenticated_principal before being captured as a pytest assertion.
